Any values that are not specified by ResStock are calculated using the defaults in the BuildResidentialHPXML OpenStudio measure. In this case, rather than using the nominal ceiling insulation R-value, OS-HPXML uses the effective R-value when constructing the ceiling assembly. Effective R-value represents the overall thermal resistance of the entire ceiling assembly, not just the insulation material. It accounts for additional layers such as drywall, air films, structural framing, and other materials that contribute to or detract from heat flow resistance. As a result, the effective R-value is typically higher than the insulation-only R-value. 8 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Results 4.1 Single Model Results This section analyzes three example dwelling units that received attic floor insulation (insulation ceiling) upgrades. These three example units represent a range of climate conditions. The floor area of these three dwelling units is different. Furthermore, the heating and cooling setpoint temperature is also different. As a result, the baseline heating and cooling energy consumption can vary across the three example dwelling units, appearing either high or low. This section does not compare absolute energy consumption among these three example dwellings. Instead, it focuses solely on the percentage energy reduction achieved by the attic floor insulation upgrade. The annual energy consumption of three example dwelling units was evaluated before and after attic floor insulation upgrade. The upgrade resulted in reductions across several heating- and cooling-related end uses, including heating, cooling, heating and cooling fan/pumps, heating heat pump backup, and associated backup fan/pumps. Results are described as follows: Dwelling unit 1 had baseline attic insulation of R-13 and was upgraded to R-49. It is located in Florida (climate zone 1A), a hot-humid region with high cooling loads and minimal heating demand). Figure 3 shows that this dwelling uses electricity for both heating and cooling. Total cooling energy consumption, including cooling and associated fan/pump energy, was reduced from 32.5 MBtu to 31.3 MBtu, a 3.7% reduction.
